review.description: Connection recovery now distinguishes accepted-result503 from unknown original mutation and terminal oversized result. Four local setup entities preserve single-use submissions and show an ambiguous-save locked state. Other unchanged direct contracts receive explicit structural reviews.
review.implementation: Reviewed bridge exact-result/no-replay handling, shared bounded finite responses and credentialForm/FormHTML context/save state. W-CONNECTION-BLOCKER owns operation/native/deadline recovery; local setup entities own the single-use key-save boundary. Stable IDs, ownership direction and pinned product adoption are preserved.
review.tests: Read the5 browser operation cases, native pipe regressions and local credential deadline assertion. UI mappings claim handler-level local-key safety only; local form browser execution and actual alternate transport acceptance remain gaps. Every current direct UI contract has a child review based on its actual mapped source/assertion ownership. The sixth browser recovery assertion distinguishes terminal provider503 from retryable transport503. Eight additional indirect package/browser-controller consumers were also inspected: actual host-bound/checksummed/mapping-refusal package assertions and owner/Host/session/Origin/CSRF controller assertions remain unchanged; their real-host gaps stay open. These indirect consumers are outside the direct mixed-review child decision set.
